summary: Circa 1942/43 Aircraft Warning Service post on the Los Padres NF, San Luis Obispo County, built and staffed by the Forest Service; register lists it as a former site, removal date unknown.

facts.design: Standard AWS post structure with a ground cabin and cupola
facts.status_note: Former Fire Lookout Sites register gives removal as unknown; the Forest Fire Lookout Association California list marks it gone; no source describes the site now

staffing.status: staffed by the US Forest Service as a WWII AWS post

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Los Padres National Forest; cooperator US Army Ground Observer Corps

events.note: Built circa 1942/43 as a standard AWS post; the register's description says constructed in 1942 or 1943
The Aircraft Warning Service it belonged to was deactivated May 29, 1944; no source gives this post's closing date
Registered April 23, 2020 as US 2042, CA 148; nominated by Brad Eells

evidence.supports: standard AWS post with ground cabin and cupola, built 1942 or 1943
evidence.quote: A standard AWS post structure with a ground cabin and cupola were constructed in 1942 or 1943.

evidence.supports: dual purpose: enemy aircraft spotting and fire detection
evidence.quote: Avenales Lookout was a dual purpose site, used for enemy aircraft spotting and fire detection.

evidence.supports: Forest Service built, provisioned and staffed the post
evidence.quote: The US Forest Service built, provisioned and staffed the post.

evidence.supports: Army reimbursed the Forest Service for all costs
evidence.quote: The US Army reimbursed the US Forest Service for all costs.

evidence.supports: operators reported aircraft activity and all fires and smoke to USFS dispatch
evidence.quote: Operators were expected to report all aircraft activities and report all fires and smokes to USFS dispatch.

evidence.supports: aircraft information was then passed on to the Army, after dispatch
evidence.quote: Aircraft information was then relayed to the Army.

evidence.supports: AWS was a civilian service of the US Army Ground Observer Corps, established to watch for enemy planes
evidence.quote: The Aircraft Warning Service (AWS) was a civilian service of the United States Army Ground Observer Corps established during World War II to keep watch for enemy planes entering American airspace.

evidence.supports: California list: Avenales AWS, San Luis Obispo, status Gone
evidence.quote: Avenales AWS San Luis Obispo 35.18922 -120.24640 AWS Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief lists 1942; the register says circa 1942/43 and, in its description, 1942 or 1943. The event year stays 1942 and the range is in the note.

notes_for_editor: Only one site-specific source: the Former Fire Lookout Sites register. The Forest Service and Army roles come from it alone. Removal date and current condition are unknown; the register says Removed Unknown. The Wikipedia article gives the national service's deactivation date only; it does not say this post closed then. A San Luis Obispo Tribune article on wildfire lookouts came up in search but timed out twice and was not read. Search budget used: 2 searches; page reads: 5 successful, one of them an OCR PDF that gave nothing usable; 2 timeouts on a newspaper article.
